skill.name: wp-plugin-development
skill.description: Develop and review WordPress plugins with guidance for architecture, hooks, lifecycle, settings, storage, cron, security, debugging, testing, and release packaging.
skill.summary: Build maintainable WordPress plugins with secure lifecycle, data, settings, and release practices.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: All 28 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, JavaScript template literals, and a bounded read-only plugin scanner. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, network activity, file writes, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: If using `$wpdb->prepare()`, avoid building queries with concatenated user input.

If this is a full site repo, pick the specific plugin under `wp-content/plugins/` or `mu-plugins/` b

- Avoid directly trusting `$_POST` / `$_GET`; use `wp_unslash()` and specific keys.
- Use `$wpdb->prepare()` for SQL; avoid building SQL with string concatenation.
- Avoid heavy side effects at file load time; load on hooks.

content.value_statement: WordPress plugin changes can introduce lifecycle, data, and security defects. This skill provides a structured workflow for implementation, review, testing, and release preparation.
actual_capabilities: Locates WordPress plugin entry points by scanning PHP plugin headers.
Guides plugin architecture, bootstrap design, hook registration, and admin-only loading.
Covers activation, deactivation, uninstall, migrations, and rewrite-rule handling.
Applies nonce, capability, sanitization, escaping, and prepared-statement guardrails.
Plans settings, data storage, cron tasks, schema upgrades, and manual triggers.
Defines checks for activation, settings, uninstall behavior, linting, tests, and asset builds.
limitations: Targets WordPress 6.9 or later and PHP 7.2.24 or later.
Requires repository access and a clearly selected target plugin before edits.
Some workflows require WP-CLI, but the skill does not install it.
Does not replace runtime testing in representative single-site and multisite environments.

use_cases.title: Create a New Plugin
use_cases.description: Design a predictable bootstrap, register hooks, add settings, and establish security checks before implementation.

use_cases.title: Secure an Existing Plugin
use_cases.description: Review request handling, permissions, nonces, output escaping, SQL queries, cron jobs, and uninstall behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Plugin Release
use_cases.description: Verify activation, settings, cleanup, migrations, tests, linting, assets, and package contents before distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository and identify the WordPress plugin entry point. Explain its structure, hooks, and immediate risks before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Secure Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a Settings API page for [options]. Include sanitization callbacks, capability checks, nonces, escaped output, and focused tests.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Plugin Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [plugin] into a minimal bootstrap and loader architecture. Preserve behavior, register lifecycle hooks correctly, and add verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Full Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [plugin] for nonce, capability, input, escaping, SQL, cron, migration, and uninstall risks. Implement fixes and run available tests.

output_examples.input: Find the plugin entry point and summarize its architecture.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the main plugin file, header metadata, loader pattern, registered hooks, admin boundaries, and files requiring review.

output_examples.input: Review the settings save flow for security problems.
output_examples.output: The review checks capability enforcement, nonce validation, explicit input keys, unslashing, sanitization callbacks, and output escaping.
The release review covers activation, migrations, settings, uninstall cleanup, linting, tests, assets, package contents, and unresolved risks.

best_practices: Select the exact plugin and confirm supported WordPress and PHP versions before changing code.
Pair nonces with capability checks, sanitize explicit inputs, and escape values at output time.
Run available tests and verify activation, settings, migrations, cron, and uninstall behavior before release.
anti_patterns: Do not place heavy side effects in the main plugin file during load.
Do not trust complete request arrays or build SQL from concatenated user input.
Do not remove stored data during deactivation or run broad cleanup without uninstall guards.

faq.question: Can this skill find plugins in a full WordPress repository?
faq.answer: Yes. The included scanner finds PHP files with plugin headers and reports relative entry-point paths.

faq.question: Does it support multisite plugins?
faq.answer: It asks for single-site or multisite context and highlights network activation, but representative multisite testing remains necessary.

faq.question: Can it create Settings API pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides registration, sections, fields, sanitization callbacks, capability checks, and escaped output.

faq.question: Does a nonce replace an authorization check?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires an appropriate capability check because nonces prevent request forgery but do not grant authorization.

faq.question: Can it manage plugin data and cron tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers options, custom tables, schema versions, idempotent cron jobs, upgrade routines, and manual triggers.

faq.question: Does it package and publish releases automatically?
faq.answer: It guides release verification and packaging checks. Publishing depends on the repository tooling and requested workflow.
